findings.title: Worktree-aware project resolution is deliberately ignored
findings.description: Description: `validateFrontmatterAction` destructures only `id` from `resolveProjectWorktree` and validates `project.projectPath`, so when invoked from inside a registered cf worktree (CWD resolution returns a `worktreeId`), the command still validates the main checkout's documents. Other mutating commands (`arch.ts:53`, `future.ts:63`, `plan.ts:43`, `slice.ts:36`, `task.ts`) route through `resolveOperationPath(project, worktreeId)`. This is an informed, documented choice — slice design 923 (D4) says "resolves the project like every other `cf` command," and the closest sibling `cf check` (check.ts) behaves identically — but for the command's stated primary use case (a pre-commit gate, squadron slice 172), a hook run inside a worktree would validate the wrong tree's `project-documents/`. Worth a follow-up decision once worktree-based gating is actually in use.

findings.title: Secondary branches of the new command lack tests
findings.description: Description: The critical paths are well covered (exit 0/1/2, JSON shape incl. `fixLog`/`fixErrors`, path forwarding, date-stamp arg, unfixable-finding pass-through). Not covered: (1) the `No projectPath configured` UserError branch (validate.ts:94-96); (2) the mixed `--fix` outcome — some findings fixed, others unfixable — which is the only case combining a non-empty `fixLog` with `remaining.length > 0`, and it's what would catch a wrong "Fixed X of Y" count or an exit-code slip (only all-fixed and all-unfixable are tested); (3) `--json` on the invocation-error path (stderr JSON with `code: PROJECT_NOT_FOUND`, exit 2). Given the command is a scripted gate, adding at least (2) would be worthwhile.

findings.title: `SEVERITY_ICON` typed wider than the severity union
findings.description: Description: `SEVERITY_ICON` is `Record<string, string>` although `FrontmatterFinding['severity']` is the closed union `'warning' | 'error'`. Typing it as `Record<FrontmatterFinding['severity'], string>` (plus the existing `?? '?'` fallback for safety) would let the compiler catch a future severity typo. Minor, and consistent with the identical pattern in check.ts:24 — fixing both together would keep them aligned.
